construct: In the ubiquitin-proteasome system, E1 activates ubiquitin, E2 carries activated ubiquitin, and E3 ubiquitin ligases provide much of the substrate specificity by recognizing target proteins and promoting ubiquitin transfer. Polyubiquitinated substrates can then be recognized and degraded by the proteasome.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: E1 activation and E2 loading remain intact, but one specific target is no longer recognized or polyubiquitinated; substrate selectivity therefore fails at the E3 ligase step.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Proteasome dysfunction could also cause target accumulation, but ubiquitination would still occur and polyubiquitinated proteins would accumulate; the stem instead shows selective failure before tagging.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The combination of preserved E1/E2 function and target-specific loss of recognition uniquely identifies the E3 ubiquitin ligase.
